content.text:
The pattern matches the NaCaMgAl(SiO3)4 pyroxene (mp-1221089) alone. I simulated seven of the nine candidates; CaSmMn2O6 and CaMn7O12 were not checked.

- **Main match:** the observed pattern has a 100 peak at 30.15° and a 57 peak at 31.1°, about 0.95° apart. The simulated pyroxene pattern has its 100/59 pair 0.9° apart near 29.75/30.65°.
- **Second match:** the observed triplet at 35.5/35.85/36.65° (intensities 22/41/49) has the same shape as the simulated triplet at about 34.9/35.2/36.0° (23/40/38).
- **Shift:** the observed peaks sit about 0.4–0.6° higher than the simulation, and the gaps between them are a little wider. That fits a lattice compressed by roughly 1%. I estimated this; I did not refine it.
- **Weaker peaks:** the observed features near 40–44° look plausible for this phase, but I did not check them peak by peak.
- **Other candidates checked:** BaBiO3, CsErO2, SnO, CsBiO2, SrRhO3 and RbAl(MoO4)2 all put strong peaks where nothing is observed, or miss the 31.1° peak. Examples are 32.3° for CsBiO2 and 26° and 32° for CsErO2.
- **Second phase:** I don't see one. Small bumps near 17.6°, 20.35° and 28.3° are close to the background noise (about 10), or could be weak reflections of the pyroxene.
